questions: Is a 5-sensor spread of ±0.02 m with 12 mm footprints too wide or too narrow for the controller to produce a clean signal? Report whether the signal saturates or dead-zones at the bends.
Does the forward sensor lead at y=0.05 m cause overshoot or oscillation on the slalom, or is the lead helpful?
Does the 0.12 m wheel track give enough turn authority at 1.5 m/s, or does the robot need more or less?
Any line-loss events on the s-bend or slalom, and at which points?

intent: Establish a symmetric, well-overlapping five-sensor baseline ahead of the axle with moderate track and body size. This gives the Integrator a clean, predictable platform to tune on the development tracks and gives me evidence for how sensor lead and spread affect line-keeping before I change anything.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Hypotheses to test: (1) a wider sensor spread reduces line loss on sharp bends at a cost in signal resolution; (2) a larger forward lead improves high-speed tracking but increases oscillation; (3) a lower mass or smaller wheel track changes how quickly the robot can correct, which matters most on the slalom. Next I want rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation from the race to test these.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet and the geometry is a baseline, not a tuned design. The baseline needs to sense the line well at the speeds the course demands. The course must be covered in under 3 s, roughly 1.5 m/s or more, so the sensors should sit ahead of the axle to give the Integrator lead time to correct bends before the wheels reach them. Five sensors spread across about ±0.02 m cover the 25 mm tape with overlap, so the reading stays informative when the robot is slightly off centre and the signal does not saturate quickly. A 12 mm footprint is a compromise: small enough to resolve the tape edge, large enough to avoid dropouts from noise. The body is mid-sized, with a wheel track of 0.12 m for moderate turn authority and a 0.03 m wheel radius for speed. Mass is 0.8 kg, which keeps yaw inertia modest for quick bends. Body width of 0.12 m gives a comfortable off-track margin: the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03), so 0.0425 m, not 0.06 m, so this margin is the binding constraint. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with few line-loss events, since the sensor baseline is symmetric and the spread is wide enough to keep the tape in view through the bends. The main risk is oscillation on the slalom from the lead distance, which I want measured.
